notes: 11 of 12 pass; the single failure is the prose lint, and it is a real one: the PR body has 7 findings and the ratelimit commit body 3, all long leads, long sentences and semicolons, which is exactly the writing-density problem the lint exists to catch, so the assertion is discriminating. Two eval-design observations. First, assertions 10 and 11 encode different thresholds for the same text: assertion 11 allows a 25-word problem lead, while prose-lint caps a paragraph lead at 20 words, so a 23-word lead (as here) passes 11 and fails 10; the author should pick one number. Second, the transcript is an executor-written summary rather than a raw tool log, so assertion 5 (tests ran before push) and the push ordering can only be verified on the executor's word; a raw command log or a check_run.py test of the marker/test artifacts would make it verifiable. Uncovered outcomes worth an assertion: the agent correctly refused to commit .env/scratch.py and flagged the missing .gitignore, and it noticed the stale body misattributes 99.1% to backoff alone; neither is scored. check_run.py already checks 'three tenants' and journal words, which no assertion lists.
